rubrics.title: General cognitive ability
rubrics.description: Learn quickly, reason about new problems, and connect ideas across domains without over-relying on memorized templates.

rubrics.title: Role-related knowledge
rubrics.description: Depth in CS fundamentals, coding, and—for mid+ levels—system design relevant to the job family.

rubrics.title: Googleyness
rubrics.description: Collaboration, humility, bias for action, user focus, and comfort with ambiguity in a team setting.

rubrics.title: Emerging leadership
rubrics.description: Influence without authority, mentoring, driving clarity, and improving team outcomes beyond individual tasks.

leadershipRubrics.title: Navigate ambiguity
leadershipRubrics.description: Structure unclear problems, align stakeholders, and deliver incremental value while requirements evolve.

leadershipRubrics.title: Drive impact
leadershipRubrics.description: Choose high-leverage work, measure outcomes, and iterate based on data and user feedback.

leadershipRubrics.title: Develop others
leadershipRubrics.description: Coach peers, share knowledge, and raise the bar through reviews, docs, and pairing.

leadershipRubrics.title: Act with integrity
leadershipRubrics.description: Escalate risks early, admit mistakes, and prioritize user trust and safety over short-term wins.

storyPrompts.title: Disagreement on technical direction
storyPrompts.prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate or manager on a technical approach. How did you handle it?

storyPrompts.title: Ambiguous project start
storyPrompts.prompt: Describe a project with unclear requirements. What did you do in the first two weeks?

storyPrompts.title: Missed deadline or incident
storyPrompts.prompt: Share a time you missed a commitment or caused a production issue. What happened and what changed afterward?

storyPrompts.title: Above-and-beyond for users
storyPrompts.prompt: When did you go out of your way to improve user experience or reliability?

storyPrompts.title: Mentoring or unblocking others
storyPrompts.prompt: Give an example of helping a teammate succeed when they were stuck.

storyPrompts.title: Prioritization under pressure
storyPrompts.prompt: Tell me about competing priorities with limited time. How did you decide what to cut?

storyPrompts.title: Learning something new fast
storyPrompts.prompt: Describe learning a new codebase, tool, or domain quickly to deliver value.

storyPrompts.title: Inclusive collaboration
storyPrompts.prompt: Share a time you ensured quieter voices or diverse perspectives were heard in a decision.

storyPrompts.title: Pushing back on scope creep
storyPrompts.prompt: When did you push back on scope or quality risks while staying collaborative?

storyPrompts.title: Data changed your mind
storyPrompts.prompt: Tell me about a decision where metrics or an experiment changed your original plan.

deliveryTips: Use STAR: Situation (10%), Task (10%), Action (60%), Result (20%) with metrics when possible.
Say “I” for your actions and “we” for team context—interviewers want your specific contribution.
Keep stories to 2–3 minutes; offer to go deeper if the interviewer probes.
Prepare 8–10 stories that map to multiple rubrics to avoid repetition across interviewers.
For failures, emphasize learning, systemic fixes, and what you do differently now.
Avoid blaming; focus on facts, trade-offs, and collaborative resolution.

englishPractice.title: Explain hash map vs tree map
englishPractice.instruction: Record a 5-minute comparison of average vs ordered map trade-offs for a Google-scale service.
englishPractice.youtubeSearch: hash map vs tree map interview explanation
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Explain when you would choose a hash map versus a balanced tree map for an in-memory index serving 10M QPS reads.

englishPractice.title: Walk through BFS vs DFS
englishPractice.instruction: Whiteboard verbally: shortest path vs connectivity; give one example each.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: A interviewer asks which traversal you pick for rotten oranges spreading—defend BFS in under 90 seconds.

englishPractice.title: Clarifying questions script
englishPractice.instruction: Practice asking 5 clarifying questions before coding Two Sum variants.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Read a vague prompt (“find pairs with sum K”) and ask constraints without solving yet.

englishPractice.title: Complexity narration
englishPractice.instruction: After solving, state time/space and whether you can optimize further.
englishPractice.youtubeSearch: how to explain time complexity interview
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Explain O(n log n) for sorting + two pointers on 3Sum without reading notes.

englishPractice.title: System design opener
englishPractice.instruction: Practice 3-minute requirements for “design a URL shortener” including scale estimates.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: List functional/non-functional requirements and one back-of-envelope QPS estimate aloud.

englishPractice.title: STAR story timing
englishPractice.instruction: Deliver one Googleyness story in exactly 150 seconds using a timer.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Tell the “disagreement on technical direction” story with one metric at the end.

englishPractice.title: Think-aloud while stuck
englishPractice.instruction: Practice narrating hypotheses when you do not know the optimal pattern yet.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: On Word Ladder, verbalize BFS setup even if implementation is slow—focus on communication.

englishPractice.title: Follow-up extension
englishPractice.instruction: Take a solved medium problem and explain the hard follow-up without coding fully.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: After Valid Parentheses, explain how you would generate all valid combinations of n pairs.

englishPractice.title: Concise project pitch
englishPractice.instruction: 90-second project summary: problem, your role, tech, impact metric.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Pitch your most recent backend project as if opening a Google phone screen.

englishPractice.title: Polite pushback phrase bank
englishPractice.instruction: Drill phrases for disagreeing respectfully and proposing experiments.
englishPractice.practicePrompt: Role-play: teammate wants microservices; you propose modular monolith—stay collaborative.
